# Kijan pou m priye? Yon gid senp pou pale ak Bondye chak jou

URL: https://shekinahsda.org/blog/kijan-pou-m-priye/
Category: Devotional
Author: Paul Edwards
Published: 2026-10-27

Ou pa bezwen bèl mo pou priye, paske Jezi te ban nou yon modèl senp, Sentespri a ede nou lè mo yo bloke, e Papa a ap tann tande vwa ou chak jou.


Petèt ou chita sou kabann ou aswè a, kay la fin trankil, epi ou santi ou ta renmen pale ak Bondye. Men lè ou fèmen je ou, mo yo pa vini. Ou mande tèt ou si gen yon fason ki kòrèk pou priye, si ou dwe di kèk mo espesyal, oswa si Bondye ap koute yon moun tankou ou. Si kesyon sa a, "Kijan pou m priye?", janm pase nan tèt ou, konnen ou pa poukont ou.

Menm disip Jezi yo te gen kesyon sa a. Yon jou, apre Jezi te fin priye, youn nan yo di l: "Lord, teach us to pray" (Lik 11:1, KJV), sa vle di "Seyè, montre nou priye." Yo te wè gen yon bagay espesyal nan fason Jezi te pale ak Papa a, epi yo te vle sa tou. Li te ba yo yon modèl, epi li te louvri kè Papa a devan yo.

Nan devosyon sa a, n ap gade sa Bib la di sou lapriyè: priyè Jezi te montre disip li yo, kisa sa vle di priye nan non Jezi, kijan pou pote enkyetid ou bay Bondye, ak sa pou fè lè ou pa konn sa pou di. Apre sa, n ap ba ou kèk etap pratik pou kòmanse jodi a menm. Ou pa bezwen gwo mo, ou sèlman bezwen yon kè ki vle pale ak Papa a.

## Repons kout la: kijan pou m priye?

Pou priye, ou pale ak Bondye tankou yon pitit ki pale ak yon Papa ki renmen l. Ou ka kòmanse pa lwanj ak remèsiman, di l sa ki nan kè ou ak tout onètete, mande l padon, prezante bezwen ou ak bezwen lòt moun, epi fini nan non Jezi. Jezi te bay Lapriyè Seyè a nan Matye 6:9 a 13 kòm yon modèl pou gide nou, pa kòm yon fòmil fèmen.

Lapriyè se pa yon egzamen ou ka echwe, se yon relasyon k ap grandi chak jou. Kwayans Fondamantal 11 Legliz Advantis Setyèm Jou a, ki rele "Growing in Christ" (Grandi nan Kris), di Bondye rele nou pou nou pase tan ak Jezi "daily in prayer", sa vle di chak jou nan lapriyè. Lè ou priye, ou pa fè Bondye yon favè. Se li menm ki envite ou vin jwenn li.

**Sa lapriyè pa ye**
- Se pa yon fòmil majik pou fè Bondye obeyi nou
- Se pa yon pèfòmans pou moun wè
- Ou pa bezwen bèl mo ni lang espesyal
- Se yon pitit k ap pale ak Papa l

## Kisa Bib la di sou fason pou nou priye?

Bib la di lapriyè se yon konvèsasyon sensè ak Bondye, pa yon spektak pou moun admire nou. Nan Matye 6, anvan Jezi bay Lapriyè Seyè a, li avèti moun ki priye pou lòt moun ka wè yo. Li envite nou chèche yon kote trankil kote nou ka rankontre Papa a kè a kè.

> "But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door, pray to thy Father which is in secret; and thy Father which seeth in secret shall reward thee openly." Matthew 6:6, KJV

Mo "closet" la vle di yon ti chanm prive anndan kay la. Jezi pa entèdi lapriyè an piblik, men li montre nou lapriyè se yon randevou ak Bondye, pa ak foul la. Nan vèsè 8 la, li ajoute yon bèl pawòl: "your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him." Papa ou deja konnen sa ou bezwen, men li toujou vle tande vwa ou.

## Kijan Jezi te montre nou priye nan Lapriyè Seyè a?

Jezi te montre nou priye lè l te ba nou yon modèl ki kòmanse ak Bondye anvan li rive sou bezwen nou. Lapriyè Seyè a kout, men li gen tout sa yon kè bezwen: lwanj, soumisyon, demann pou chak jou, padon, ak pwoteksyon. Men pawòl yo jan yo ye nan King James Version an.

> "After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen." Matthew 6:9 to 13, KJV

Men yon parafraz an kreyòl, se pa yon tradiksyon ofisyèl: Papa nou ki nan syèl la, se pou tout moun respekte non ou kòm yon non ki sen. Se pou wayòm ou vini, se pou volonte ou fèt sou tè a menm jan li fèt nan syèl la. Ban nou manje nou bezwen pou jodi a, padone nou peche nou jan nou padone moun ki fè nou mal. Pa kite nou tonbe anba tantasyon, men delivre nou anba sa ki mal, paske wayòm nan, pouvwa a, ak glwa a se pou ou pou tout tan.

- 5 : vèsè nan Lapriyè Seyè a
- 2 : fwa Jezi di "in my name"
- 7:30 PM : lapriyè madi ak mèkredi

Remake premye mo yo: "Our Father", Papa nou, pa "Papa m" sèlman. Lè ou priye, ou fè pati yon fanmi ki pi gran pase kay ou. Tablo sa a ka ede ou kite chak pati nan priyè a gide pwòp pawòl pa ou.

| Pati nan priyè a | Sa li montre nou | Kijan pou m priye l jodi a |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Papa nou ki nan syèl la | Bondye se yon Papa ki pre | Rele l Papa ak konfyans |
| Non ou se yon non ki sen | Lwanj ak respè an premye | Di l mèsi pou kiyès li ye |
| Wayòm ou vini, volonte ou fèt | Nou mete plan nou anba men l | Mande l dirije desizyon ou |
| Ban nou pen nou chak jou | Bondye okipe bezwen nou | Pale l de bezwen jodi a |
| Padone nou jan nou padone | Konfesyon ak padon | Nonmen moun ou bezwen padone |
| Delivre nou anba sa ki mal | Pwoteksyon ak fòs | Mande l kenbe ou fèm |

## Kisa sa vle di priye nan non Jezi?

Priye nan non Jezi vle di nou pwoche bò kote Papa a sou baz sa Jezi fè pou nou, pa sou baz pwòp merit pa nou. Se yon fason pou di: "Papa, m ap vin jwenn ou paske Jezi louvri chemen an pou mwen." Jezi li menm te bay pwomès sa a bay disip li yo.

> "And whatsoever ye shall ask in my name, that will I do, that the Father may be glorified in the Son. If ye shall ask any thing in my name, I will do it." John 14:13 to 14, KJV

Remake objektif pwomès la: "that the Father may be glorified in the Son", pou Papa a ka resevwa glwa nan Pitit la. Mande nan non Jezi vle di mande sa ki dakò ak karaktè li ak volonte li. Lè nou di "nan non Jezi, amèn", nou ap di nou fè l konfyans pou repons lan, kèlkeswa jan l vini. Se pa fòs lapriyè nou ki sove nou, se Jezi.

## Kijan pou m priye lè m enkyete?

Lè ou enkyete, Bib la envite ou pote chak enkyetid bay Bondye nan lapriyè, ak remèsiman, epi kite lapè li veye sou kè ou. Apot Pòl te ekri pawòl sa yo bay legliz Filip la pandan li te nan prizon. Li pa t konnen kijan ka li a t ap fini, men li te konnen kiyès ki te kenbe l.

> "Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus." Philippians 4:6 to 7, KJV

"Be careful for nothing" vle di pa enkyete pou anyen. Pwomès la se pa ke tout pwoblèm ap disparèt menm jou a, men lapè Bondye ap kanpe tankou yon gad devan kè nou ak lespri nou. Si se lajan, sante, fanmi, oswa papye imigrasyon ki fè ou pa ka dòmi, ou gen dwa nonmen yo youn pa youn devan Bondye.

Related: [Stress Less: Trusting God With Your Worries](https://shekinahsda.org/blog/stress-less-trusting-god-with-your-worries/)

## Kisa pou m fè lè m pa konn sa pou m di nan lapriyè?

Lè ou pa konn sa pou di, ou ka toujou vin devan Bondye ak silans ou, dlo nan je ou, oswa yon sèl mo, paske Sentespri a ede nou priye. Gen moman lavi a tèlman lou, mo yo bloke nan gòj nou. Bib la pa fè nou wont pou sa, li ban nou yon pwomès ki pote rekonfò.

> "Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmities: for we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered." Romans 8:26, KJV

Sentespri a "maketh intercession for us", li entèsede pou nou ak soupi ki pa ka eksprime ak pawòl. Sa vle di yon "Seyè, ede m" ki soti nan fon kè ou se yon lapriyè tout bon. Kwayans Fondamantal 11 la di tou ke Sentespri a "dwells within us and empowers us", li rete anndan nou epi li ban nou fòs.

Si ou santi Bondye pa reponn ou, pa kite sa fè ou kanpe. Anpil moun nan Bib la te pase menm sezon sa a, epi Bondye te rete fidèl avèk yo. Devosyon sa a an anglè ka ankouraje ou.

Related: [When Prayer Feels Quiet](https://shekinahsda.org/blog/when-prayer-feels-quiet/)

## Ki lapriyè pou m fè chak jou?

Ou ka fè yon lapriyè chak jou ki senp: chwazi yon lè fiks, kòmanse ak lwanj, di Bondye verite a, mande nan non Jezi, epi pran yon ti tan pou li Pawòl li. Pa chèche fè l pafè, chèche fè l chak jou. Jezi te di nan Lik 11:9, "Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you." Men senk etap pou ede ou kòmanse semèn sa a.

- Chwazi yon moman : Maten bonè oswa anvan ou dòmi, menm si se senk minit
- Kòmanse ak lwanj : Di Bondye mèsi pou yon bagay presi li fè pou ou
- Di l verite a : Pale l de kè ou, pè ou, ak peche ou san kache anyen
- Mande nan non Jezi : Prezante bezwen ou ak bezwen lòt moun, epi fè l konfyans
- Koute Pawòl la : Li yon ti pasaj nan Bib la epi kite l pale ak ou

Ou ka fè etap sa yo an kreyòl oswa an anglè, poukont ou oswa ak pitit ou. Bondye konprann tout lang, e yon "Mèsi, Jezi" ki soti nan bouch yon timoun gen valè devan li. Ti abitid sa yo bati yon lafwa ki ka kanpe lè tanpèt yo vini.

## Kesyon moun konn poze

### Èske gen yon bon ak yon move fason pou priye?

Pa gen yon sèl fòmil ki obligatwa, men Bib la montre bon lapriyè sòti nan yon kè sensè ki pa chèche moun wè l. Nan Matye 6:7, Jezi avèti nou kont "vain repetitions", sa vle di repete mo san kè nou pa ladan. Ou ka itilize Lapriyè Seyè a, pwòp mo pa ou, oswa toude.

### Konbyen tan mwen dwe pase nan lapriyè?

Bib la pa bay yon kantite minit fiks, men li envite nou rete an kontak ak Bondye tout jounen an. Nan 1 Tesalonisyen 5:17, Pòl di nou priye san rete, sa vle di viv ak kè nou toujou tounen vè Bondye. Kòmanse ak yon ti tan ou ka kenbe chak jou, menm si se dis minit, epi kite l grandi.

### Èske Bondye tande lapriyè m fè nan kè m san m pa pale fò?

Wi, Bondye tande lapriyè ou fè nan kè ou menm si pèsonn pa tande vwa ou. Jezi di nan Matye 6:6 ke Papa a "seeth in secret", li wè sa ki an kachèt. Women 8:26 montre Sentespri a konprann menm soupi nou pa ka mete an mo. Kidonk ou ka priye nan machin, nan travay, oswa nan mitan nwit lan, epi Bondye ap tande ou.

## Kesyon pou reflechi

Pran kèk minit trankil pou reflechi sou kesyon sa yo, poukont ou oswa ak fanmi ou. Ki pati nan Lapriyè Seyè a ou pi bezwen priye jodi a, epi poukisa? Ki enkyetid ou te kenbe pou tèt ou ke ou ta ka depoze devan Bondye aswè a? Ki moun nan lavi ou ou ta ka priye pou li semèn sa a, menm si li pa janm konnen ou te fè sa?

## Yon pawòl ankourajman

Pa kite pè fè erè anpeche ou priye. Bondye pa ap tann pou ou vin pafè anvan ou pale avè l, li ap tann ou jan ou ye a. Menm Papa ki te kenbe Pòl nan prizon an ap koute ou jodi a nan chanm ou, nan machin ou, oswa nan kizin ou. Li fè nou yon pwomès klè nan liv Jeremi.

> "Call unto me, and I will answer thee, and shew thee great and mighty things, which thou knowest not." Jeremiah 33:3, KJV

Nan Jeremi 33:3, Bondye pa di "si ou konn priye byen, m ap reponn ou". Li di senpleman, "rele m". Chak fwa ou di "Papa", ou ap fè yon pa pi pre kè li.

## Yon lapriyè

Papa nou ki nan syèl la, mèsi paske ou envite nou pale avè ou tankou pitit ki pale ak papa yo. Lè nou pa konn sa pou nou di, kite Sentespri ou priye pou nou ak soupi ki pi fon pase mo nou. Pran enkyetid nou yo, padone peche nou yo, epi kite lapè ou veye sou kè nou ak lespri nou. Montre nou priye chak jou, non pa pou moun wè nou, men pou nou ka konnen ou pi byen. Nan non Jezi nou priye, amèn.

## Pwochen etap ou

Si gen yon bagay ki chita lou sou kè ou jodi a, ou pa bezwen pote l poukont ou. Fanmi legliz nou an t ap kontan priye avè ou ak pou ou, epi ou ka voye yon demann lapriyè sou paj demann lapriyè nou an. Ou envite tou pou vin priye avè nou nan reyinyon lapriyè Legliz Advantis Setyèm Jou Ayisyen Shekinah nan Alvarado, Texas, sou Zoom chak madi ak mèkredi aswè a 7:30 PM. N ap adore an kreyòl ak an anglè, e gen yon plas pou ou nan mitan nou.

- Source: [Matthew 6:5 to 13 (King James Version, Bible.com)](https://www.bible.com/bible/1/MAT.6.5-13.KJV)

- Source: [Luke 11:1 to 13 (King James Version, Bible.com)](https://www.bible.com/bible/1/LUK.11.1-13.KJV)

- Source: [John 14:13 to 14 (KJV, Christianity.com)](https://www.christianity.com/bible/kjv/john/14-13-14)

- Source: [Philippians 4 (King James Version, Bible.com)](https://www.bible.com/bible/1/PHP.4.kjv)

- Source: [Romans 8:26 (King James Bible Online)](https://www.kingjamesbibleonline.org/Romans-8-26/)

- Source: [Jeremiah 33:3 (King James Version, Bible.com)](https://bible.com/bible/1/JER.33.3-11.KJV)

- Source: [How to Grow in Christ Every Day, Fundamental Belief 11 (Seventh-day Adventist Church)](https://adventist.org/beliefs/official/growing-in-christ)

> "Call unto me, and I will answer thee, and shew thee great and mighty things, which thou knowest not." Jeremiah 33:3, KJV

# Kisa Bib la di sou Saba a? Jou Saba nan Bib la

URL: https://shekinahsda.org/blog/kisa-bib-la-di-sou-saba-a/
Category: Bible Answers
Author: Jack Thompson
Published: 2026-10-27

Yon etid cho e klè sou sa Bib la di sou jou Saba a depi kreyasyon an rive nan lavi Jezi, poukisa Advantis Setyèm Jou yo adore Samdi, ak kijan Saba a ka vin yon kado pou fanmi w.


Se Vandredi swa, solèy la ap desann dousman, epi ou tande yon vwazen ki di ak kè kontan: "Saba a rive!" Ou menm, ou fèk soti travay, ou fatige, epi yon kesyon rete nan tèt ou. Poukisa gen moun ki trete jou Samdi tankou yon jou ki apa? Èske se yon koutim moun envante, oswa èske se vre Bib la ki pale de sa?

Petèt kesyon an soti pi pre lakay ou toujou. Ou te grandi nan yon fanmi ki konn ale legliz jou Dimanch, epi kounye a yon zanmi envite w nan yon Legliz Advantis Setyèm Jou jou Samdi. Oswa ou se yon paran ki vle eksplike pitit ou poukisa fanmi an pa al nan mache jou Samdi. Kèlkeswa sa ki mennen w isit la, kesyon ou a bon anpil, epi Bondye pa fache lè nou chèche konprann Pawòl li.

Nan atik sa a, n ap louvri Bib la ansanm pou n wè kisa li di sou jou Saba a depi nan kreyasyon an rive nan lavi Jezi, epi menm nan syèl ak tè nouvo a. N ap separe byen klè sa Bib la di dirèkteman ak sa ki se entèpretasyon. N ap pale tou ak respè pou frè ak sè kretyen ki wè kesyon sa a yon lòt jan, paske objektif nou se pa genyen yon diskisyon, men se konnen Bondye pi byen.

## Repons kout la

- 7yèm : Jou Bondye beni nan Jenèz 2
- 4yèm : Kòmandman ki di sonje Saba a
- 20 : Kwayans Fondamantal sou Saba a

Bib la anseye ke Saba a se setyèm jou semèn nan, sa vle di jou Samdi, ki kòmanse Vandredi lè solèy kouche epi ki fini Samdi lè solèy kouche. Bondye te repoze jou sa a apre kreyasyon an, li te beni l, li te mete l apa (Jenèz 2:2 rive 3). Pita li mete l nan Dis Kòmandman yo (Egzòd 20:8 rive 11). Jezi menm te gen abitid adore jou Saba a, epi li te rele tèt li "Seyè Saba a."

Se sa Legliz Advantis Setyèm Jou kwè tou. Kwayans Fondamantal 20, ki rele "The Sabbath" sou sit ofisyèl adventist.org, di ke Kreyatè a te "rested on the seventh day" epi li te bay Saba a pou tout moun tankou yon "memorial of Creation." Kwayans lan rele Saba a "a day of delightful communion with God and one another," sa vle di yon jou kominyon ki bay kè kontan ak Bondye ak youn lòt. Rès atik la montre ki kote nan Bib la konviksyon sa yo soti.

## Kisa Bib la di sou Saba a nan kreyasyon an?

Bib la montre ke Saba a te kòmanse nan kreyasyon an, anvan pèp Izrayèl la te egziste, anvan Moyiz, epi anvan nenpòt peche. Premye fwa nou wè setyèm jou a, se pa yon lwa ki ekri sou wòch, men se yon kado Bondye bay moun li fèk kreye. Sa enpòtan anpil, paske sa vle di Saba a pa t yon fado pou yon sèl nasyon, men yon benediksyon pou tout limanite.

> "And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made. And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because that in it he had rested from all his work which God created and made." Genesis 2:2 to 3, KJV

Nan pasaj sa a, Bib la di twa bagay klè sou setyèm jou a. Bondye te repoze ladan l, Bondye te beni l, epi Bondye te sanktifye l, sa vle di li te mete l apa pou yon objektif sen. Bondye pa t repoze paske li te bouke, paske Ezayi 40:28 di li pa janm fatige. Li te repoze pou l ban nou yon modèl, epi pou l envite nou antre nan yon relasyon avè l chak semèn. Lè nou kenbe Saba a, nou di ak tout lavi nou: se Bondye ki kreye m, mwen pa yon machin ki fèt sèlman pou travay.

### Poukisa Bondye te beni yon jou olye de yon kote?

Bondye te chwazi beni yon moman nan tan an olye de yon mòn oswa yon tanp. Nenpòt moun, kèlkeswa kote li rete, ka antre nan Saba a, paske tan an rive jwenn tout moun menm jan. Yon fanmi nan Pòtoprens, yon etidyan nan Miami, ak yon travayè nan Alvarado, Texas, ka rankontre Bondye nan menm jou sen an. Se yon bèl fason Bondye montre ke lanmou li pa limite a yon sèl pèp oswa yon sèl peyi.

## Kisa Dis Kòmandman yo di sou jou Saba a?

Katriyèm kòmandman an mande nou sonje jou Saba a pou nou kenbe l pou Bondye, epi li bay rezon an: paske Bondye te kreye syèl la ak tè a nan sis jou epi li te repoze setyèm jou a. Kòmandman sa a se sèl nan dis yo ki kòmanse ak mo "sonje," tankou si Bondye te konnen nou t ap gen tandans bliye l. Li pa entwodui yon bagay nouvo, men li raple yon bagay ki te la depi nan kòmansman.

> "Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work: But the seventh day is the sabbath of the LORD thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates: For in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that in them is, and rested the seventh day: wherefore the LORD blessed the sabbath day, and hallowed it." Exodus 20:8 to 11, KJV

Remake ki jan kòmandman sa a jenere. Li pa sèlman pou papa ak manman, men pou pitit yo, pou moun k ap travay pou yo, pou bèt yo, e menm pou etranje ki lakay yo. Nan yon monn kote anpil moun travay san rete, Bondye mete yon limit ki pwoteje tout moun, sitou moun ki pi fèb yo. Saba a se tankou yon pòt Bondye louvri chak semèn pou di: ou gen dwa poze, ou gen valè menm lè ou pa pwodui anyen.

Nan liv Detewonòm, lè Moyiz repete kòmandman an, li ajoute yon lòt rezon: Bondye te delivre pèp la anba esklavaj an Ejip (Detewonòm 5:12 rive 15, parafraz an Kreyòl). Konsa Saba a se non sèlman yon souvni kreyasyon an, men tou yon souvni liberasyon. Pou nou menm ki gen istwa ayisyen nan san nou, nou konprann byen kisa sa vle di pou yon Bondye ki renmen libète ba ou yon jou kote pèsonn pa ka fè w travay tankou yon esklav.

## Èske Jezi te kenbe jou Saba a?

Wi, Levanjil yo montre klè ke Jezi te gen abitid ale nan sinagòg jou Saba a pou adore ak pou li Pawòl Bondye. Li pa t fè sa yon fwa pa aza, men se te koutim li, sa vle di yon bagay li te fè regilyèman. Lik di nou sa dirèkteman.

> "And he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up: and, as his custom was, he went into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and stood up for to read." Luke 4:16, KJV

Men Jezi pa t kenbe Saba a jan kèk chèf relijye nan epòk li te vle l kenbe l. Yo te ajoute anpil règ moun te envante, tankou entèdi moun keyi kèk grenn manje lè yo grangou oswa geri yon malad jou Saba. Jezi te geri moun jou Saba a plizyè fwa, epi li te di ke li bon pou fè byen jou sa a (Matye 12:12, parafraz an Kreyòl). Li pa t aboli Saba a, li te retire chay moun te mete sou li pou l remete l jan Bondye te vle l depi nan kòmansman.

> "And he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath: Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath." Mark 2:27 to 28, KJV

Nan de vèsè sa yo, Jezi bay de verite ki mache ansanm. Premye a, Saba a te fèt pou byen moun, pa pou fè moun soufri; se yon kado, pa yon prizon. Dezyèm lan, Jezi se Seyè Saba a, sa vle di li gen otorite sou li paske se li menm ki te kreye l ak Papa a. Lè yon moun kenbe Saba a, li pa swiv yon tradisyon vid, men li pase tan ak Seyè Saba a an pèsòn.

### Kisa disip yo te fè apre lanmò Jezi?

Apre Jezi te mouri sou lakwa jou Vandredi, fanm ki te swiv li yo te prepare epis pou kò li, men yo te tann. Menm nan doulè ak tristès yo, yo pa t bliye sa Bondye te mande. Lik di yo te repoze jou Saba a dapre kòmandman an, epi se premye jou semèn nan, jou Dimanch maten, yo te retounen bò tonbo a (Lik 24:1, parafraz an Kreyòl).

> "And they returned, and prepared spices and ointments; and rested the sabbath day according to the commandment." Luke 23:56, KJV

Vèsè sa a gen anpil valè pou kesyon nou an. Lik te ekri Levanjil li plizyè ane apre rezireksyon an, epi li toujou rele jou repo a "the sabbath day according to the commandment." Li pa di kòmandman an te fini lè Jezi mouri. Liv Travay Apot yo, ke Lik te ekri tou, montre Pòl ki te konn ale nan sinagòg jou Saba a pou preche Levanjil la (Travay 17:2, parafraz an Kreyòl).

## Saba a nan Bib la depi kòmansman rive nan fen

Lè nou gade tout Bib la ansanm, nou wè Saba a parèt nan chak gwo etap istwa delivrans lan. Li pa yon detay ki parèt yon sèl kote, men yon fil lò ki travèse Ansyen ak Nouvo Testaman. Men kèk etap kle pou ede w wè foto a an antye.

- Kreyasyon: Bondye repoze epi li beni setyèm jou a: Jenèz 2:2 rive 3

- Nan dezè a: Bondye bay lamàn sis jou epi li rete jou Saba a: Egzòd 16

- Mòn Sinayi: Saba a vin katriyèm kòmandman an: Egzòd 20:8 rive 11

- Lavi Jezi: Jezi adore jou Saba a epi li geri moun: Lik 4:16

- Apre lakwa: Fanm yo repoze dapre kòmandman an: Lik 23:56

- Syèl ak tè nouvo: Tout moun ap vin adore devan Bondye: Ezayi 66:23

Dènye etap la espesyalman bèl, paske li montre kote istwa a ap mache. Ezayi pale de yon tan kote Bondye fè syèl ak tè nouvo, epi li di ke moun ap vin adore devan l depi yon Saba rive nan yon lòt. Pwomès sa a fè nou wè Saba a pa sèlman nan sot pase a.

> "And it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith the LORD." Isaiah 66:23, KJV

Ezayi t ap pale ak pèp li nan langaj epòk li, kote nouvo lalin te make kalandriye a, kidonk nou dwe li vèsè sa a ak imilite. Sa ki klè sepandan, se ke Saba a pa parèt tankou yon bagay ki pral disparèt, men tankou yon moman adorasyon ki gen plas li nan avni Bondye prepare a. Saba a ki te kòmanse nan jaden Edenn nan gen yon plas nan tè nouvo a tou.

## Ki siy Saba a ye ant Bondye ak pèp li?

Bib la di Saba a se yon siy ant Bondye ak pèp li, ki montre se Bondye ki sanktifye yo, sa vle di se li ki fè yo sen. Ezekyèl raple pèp la mesaj sa a pandan yon peryòd difisil nan istwa yo, lè anpil nan yo te bliye Bondye. Menm lè sa a, Bondye pa t abandone siy li te ba yo a.

> "Moreover also I gave them my sabbaths, to be a sign between me and them, that they might know that I am the LORD that sanctify them." Ezekiel 20:12, KJV

Remake ke se pa pèp la ki sanktifye tèt li lè l kenbe Saba a. Se Bondye ki fè travay la; Saba a se siy ki montre nou fè l konfyans pou travay sa a. Se poutèt sa Kwayans Fondamantal 20 rele Saba a "a symbol of our redemption in Christ" ak "God's perpetual sign of His eternal covenant between Him and His people." Nou pa kenbe Saba a pou nou sove, nou kenbe l paske nou deja resevwa lagras Bondye nan Jezi Kris, epi nou vle pase tan avè l.

**Sa Bib la di dirèkteman ak sa ki se entèpretasyon**
- Bib la di dirèkteman: Bondye te beni epi sanktifye setyèm jou a (Jenèz 2:3)
- Bib la di dirèkteman: katriyèm kòmandman an mande nou sonje jou Saba a (Egzòd 20:8)
- Bib la di dirèkteman: Jezi te gen koutim adore jou Saba a (Lik 4:16)
- Entèpretasyon Advantis: kòmandman sa a toujou valab pou kretyen jodi a, tankou lòt nèf yo
- Entèpretasyon Advantis: Saba a se yon siy fidelite ak Kreyatè a nan dènye tan yo

Related: [Why Do Seventh-day Adventists Worship on Saturday?](https://shekinahsda.org/blog/why-do-seventh-day-adventists-worship-on-saturday/)

## Poukisa Advantis yo adore jou Samdi?

Advantis Setyèm Jou yo adore jou Samdi paske yo kwè setyèm jou semèn nan se jou Bondye te beni nan kreyasyon an, se jou li mete nan Dis Kòmandman yo, epi se jou Jezi menm te adore. Yo pa jwenn okenn vèsè nan Bib la kote Bondye transfere benediksyon setyèm jou a sou premye jou semèn nan. Se poutèt sa yo chwazi rete ak jou Bib la nonmen an.

Sa pa vle di Advantis yo kwè se sèlman yo menm ki renmen Bondye. Gen kretyen fidèl nan anpil legliz ki adore jou Dimanch ak tout kè yo, epi Bondye konnen kè chak moun. Diferans lan se pa sou ki moun ki pi bon, men sou kesyon sa a: kisa Bib la di? Lè nou poze kesyon sa a avèk onètete, nou envite chak moun etidye pou tèt li, avèk lapriyè, epi kite Lespri Sen an gide l.

Pou ede w wè diferans ki genyen ant jou yo nan Bib la, men yon ti tablo senp. Chak liy poze yon kesyon epi li montre ki kote nan Bib la ou ka jwenn repons lan. Pran tan pou w li chak referans nan pwòp Bib ou.

| Kesyon | Sa Bib la montre | Referans |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ki jou Bondye te beni nan kreyasyon an? | Setyèm jou a | Jenèz 2:3 |
| Ki jou kòmandman an rele Saba Seyè a? | Setyèm jou a | Egzòd 20:10 |
| Ki jou Jezi te konn ale nan sinagòg? | Jou Saba a | Lik 4:16 |
| Ki jou Jezi te leve vivan? | Premye jou semèn nan | Lik 24:1 |
| Èske gen vèsè ki chanje jou Saba a? | Okenn vèsè pa di sa | Tout Bib la |

## Kòman pou nou kenbe Saba a jodi a?

Bib la montre ke kenbe Saba a se sitou yon kesyon relasyon: kite travay ak enkyetid nou sou kote pou nou pase tan ak Bondye, ak fanmi nou, ak frè ak sè nou nan lafwa. Ezayi bay yon bèl foto sou kijan Bondye vle nou wè jou sa a. Li pa pale de yon jou tris, men de yon jou ki gen onè ak lajwa.

> "If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy pleasure on my holy day; and call the sabbath a delight, the holy of the LORD, honourable; and shalt honour him, not doing thine own ways, nor finding thine own pleasure, nor speaking thine own words:" Isaiah 58:13, KJV

Mo kle nan vèsè sa a se "a delight," sa vle di yon plezi, yon bagay ki fè kè w kontan. Bondye pa vle Saba a vin yon lis entèdiksyon ki fè timoun yo tris oswa ki fè granmoun yo santi yo nan prizon. Li vle nou santi n ap antre nan prezans yon Papa ki renmen nou, ki envite nou kite bagay pa nou yo sou kote pou nou jwenn sa ki pi bon an. Lè nou fè sa, nou dekouvri ke Saba a pa retire anyen nan lavi nou, li ajoute.

### Ki lè Saba a kòmanse e ki lè li fini?

Saba a kòmanse Vandredi lè solèy kouche epi li fini Samdi lè solèy kouche. Nan Bib la, yon jou kòmanse nan aswè, jan nou wè nan Jenèz 1 kote aswè a vini anvan maten an pou fòme premye jou a. Levitik 23:32 ak Mak 1:32 montre tou ke jou yo te konte depi yon aswè rive nan yon lòt aswè (parafraz an Kreyòl). Se poutèt sa anpil fanmi Advantis kòmanse Saba a ak yon ti tan lapriyè ak chante lè solèy la ap kouche Vandredi.

Men kèk etap pratik ki ka ede w ak fanmi w kòmanse viv Saba a kòm yon kado olye de yon chay. Pa eseye fè tout bagay yon sèl kou. Kòmanse ak yon ti pa, epi kite Bondye grandi plezi Saba a nan kè w.

- Prepare davans : Fè pwovizyon, netwaye, epi fini travay ou Vandredi pou Saba a jwenn ou pare
- Akeyi Saba a : Rasanble fanmi an lè solèy kouche Vandredi pou chante, li yon pasaj, epi priye
- Adore ansanm : Patisipe nan Lekòl Saba ak sèvis adorasyon an ak frè ak sè w yo
- Pase tan ak moun : Pataje yon repa, vizite yon malad, oswa fè yon ti mache nan lanati
- Fèmen ak lapriyè : Lè solèy kouche Samdi, remèsye Bondye pou repo li te ba ou

## Kesyon moun poze souvan

### Èske Saba a se jou Samdi oswa jou Dimanch?

Dapre Bib la, Saba a se setyèm jou semèn nan, ki se jou Samdi nan kalandriye nou jodi a. Jou Dimanch se premye jou semèn nan, jou Jezi te leve vivan, men Bib la pa janm rele Dimanch "Saba" ni li pa bay okenn kòmandman pou adore jou sa a olye de setyèm jou a. Se pou sa Legliz Advantis Setyèm Jou kontinye adore jou Samdi. Anpil kretyen bay Dimanch valè poutèt rezireksyon an, epi nou respekte sensè yo, men nou chwazi swiv jou Bib la nonmen dirèkteman.

### Èske Saba a te sèlman pou pèp jwif la?

Non, Bib la montre Saba a te bay depi nan kreyasyon an, anpil syèk anvan Abraram oswa nasyon Izrayèl la te egziste. Jezi te di "the sabbath was made for man," e mo li itilize a vle di limanite an jeneral. Ezayi 56:6 rive 7 pale tou de etranje ki atache tèt yo ak Seyè a epi ki kenbe Saba a, epi Bondye pwomèt pou l fè yo kontan lakay li (parafraz an Kreyòl). Kwayans Fondamantal 20 di menm bagay la lè li anseye ke Bondye te bay Saba a pou tout moun kòm yon souvni kreyasyon an.

### Èske Jezi oswa apot yo te chanje jou Saba a?

Pa gen okenn pasaj nan Nouvo Testaman an kote Jezi oswa apot yo di setyèm jou a pa sen ankò oswa kote yo transfere Saba a sou Dimanch. Jezi te kenbe Saba a, fanm ki te swiv li yo te repoze dapre kòmandman an apre lanmò li, epi Pòl te kontinye preche nan sinagòg jou Saba a. Advantis yo kwè adorasyon jou Dimanch te vin antre nan legliz la pita, atravè tradisyon moun, pa atravè yon kòmandman Bib la. Sa se yon konklizyon sou istwa ke chak moun ka etidye pou tèt li avèk lapriyè.

### Kisa Kolosyen 2:16 vle di sou Saba a?

Kolosyen 2:16 rive 17 di pa kite pèsonn jije nou sou manje, bwason, fèt, nouvo lalin, oswa saba yo, paske bagay sa yo se lonbraj bagay ki t ap vini, men reyalite a se nan Kris (parafraz an Kreyòl). Advantis yo, ansanm ak anpil etidyan Bib la, konprann pasaj sa a ap pale de fèt seremoni ak saba anyèl ki te nan lwa Moyiz la, ki te montre lonbraj travay Kris la. Saba setyèm jou a, li menm, te kòmanse nan kreyasyon an anvan peche, kidonk li pa t yon lonbraj ki montre lakwa. Sa se yon entèpretasyon, e nou envite w li tout chapit la nan kontèks li pou w wè sa Pòl t ap reponn.

### Èske yon moun ki pa kenbe Saba a ka sove?

Delivrans se yon kado lagras Bondye ke nou resevwa pa lafwa nan Jezi Kris, pa yon rekonpans pou bon zèv nou, menm kenbe Saba a. Efezyen 2:8 rive 9 di nou sove pa lagras atravè lafwa, epi se pa yon bagay ki soti nan nou (parafraz an Kreyòl). Bondye konnen kè chak moun ak limyè chak moun resevwa. Advantis yo kenbe Saba a kòm yon repons lanmou pou yon Sovè ki deja sove yo, pa kòm yon fason pou yo touche syèl la.

## Kisa Saba a vle di pou ou jodi a?

Apre nou fin wè tout pasaj sa yo, kesyon an vin pi pèsonèl: kisa Bondye ap di m atravè jou sa a? Pou yon manman ki travay de djòb, Saba a se pwomès ke li gen dwa poze san li pa santi l koupab. Pou yon jèn moun ki santi l pèdi nan bwi rezo sosyal yo, Saba a se yon envitasyon pou fèmen telefòn nan epi tande vwa Bondye. Pou yon fanmi ki gen tan pa jwenn tan ansanm, Saba a se yon randevou chak semèn kote tout moun chita bò tab la.

Liv Ebre yo pale de yon repo ki rete pou pèp Bondye a, yon repo ki pi fon pase yon jou san travay. Repo sa a se konfyans nan travay Bondye fè pou nou. Ekriven an itilize Saba a pou montre nou ki jan pou nou poze nan lagras Bondye.

> "There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God. For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his." Hebrews 4:9 to 10, KJV

Saba a chak semèn se tankou yon ti fenèt sou repo sa a. Lè nou sispann travay nou, nou raple tèt nou ke se pa efò nou ki sove nou, men se Jezi ki te di sou lakwa: tout bagay fini (Jan 19:30, parafraz an Kreyòl). Konsa Saba a mennen nou tounen bò kote kreyasyon an nan kòmansman, bò kote lakwa nan mitan, ak bò kote syèl ak tè nouvo a nan fen.

Related: [Resting in His Presence: What the Sabbath Teaches Us About Trust](https://shekinahsda.org/blog/resting-in-his-presence-what-the-sabbath-teaches-us-about-trust/)

## Kesyon pou reflechi

Ki sa ki pi difisil pou ou lè w panse a kite travay ak enkyetid ou sou kote pandan yon jou antye chak semèn? Si Bondye te rele Saba a "a delight," kisa ou ta ka chanje nan fason ou pase Samdi pou li vin yon jou kè kontan pou ou ak fanmi w? Ki moun nan lavi w ki bezwen tande ke Bondye ofri l repo, epi kòman ou ta ka pataje bon nouvèl sa a avè l avèk dousè?

## Yon pawòl ankourajman

Si atik sa a leve plis kesyon pase repons nan kè w, pa enkyete w. Bondye pa mande w konprann tout bagay yon sèl kou; li mande w mache avè l yon pa apre lòt. Menm Jezi te pran tan pou l eksplike disip li yo verite sou Saba a, epi li te fè sa avèk pasyans ak lanmou. Saba a se pa yon pòt fèmen pou moun ki pa konnen tout repons yo, men yon pòt louvri pou nenpòt moun ki fatige epi ki vle jwenn repo nan Bondye.

## Yon lapriyè

Papa nou ki nan syèl la, mèsi paske ou te kreye nou epi ou te ban nou yon jou pou nou repoze nan prezans ou. Ede nou wè Saba a jan ou wè l, tankou yon kado ak yon plezi, pa tankou yon chay. Louvri je nou pou nou konprann Pawòl ou, epi ban nou kouraj pou nou swiv li avèk lanmou. Mèsi pou Jezi, Seyè Saba a, ki ban nou vrè repo pou nanm nou. Nou priye nan non li, amèn.

## Pwochen etap ou

Saba a touche anpil lòt verite nan Bib la, tankou kreyasyon an, lalwa Bondye, lagras, ak retou Jezi, epi li pi fasil pou etidye l ak yon Bib louvri ak yon moun bò kote w. Si ou ta renmen etidye sa Bib la di sou Saba a pi an pwofondè, mande yon etid biblik gratis anba a. Yon moun nan Legliz Advantis Setyèm Jou Ayisyen Shekinah nan Alvarado, Texas, ap kontan etidye avè w an Kreyòl oswa an Anglè, nan ritm pa w, san okenn presyon.

Epi si ou ta renmen fè eksperyans yon Saba ak nou, ou envite lakay nou nan 205 E Carver St nan Alvarado. Lekòl Saba kòmanse Samdi a 10:00 AM, Sèvis Divin nan a 11:00 AM, epi nou adore an Kreyòl ak an Anglè. Apre sèvis la, fanmi legliz la pataje yon repa ansanm, epi ou ka chita avèk nou. Si ou pa ka vini an pèsòn, ou ka swiv adorasyon an dirèk sou YouTube.

# Giving Thanks When Life Is Hard: Bible Verses About Gratitude

URL: https://shekinahsda.org/blog/giving-thanks-when-life-is-hard/
Category: Devotional
Author: Rachel Simmons
Published: 2026-10-26

Some of the strongest words of thanks in Scripture were spoken in prison, hunger, and loss, and they can teach us to give thanks in every season, not only the easy ones.


The table is set, the house smells like something good, and everyone is supposed to be grateful. Yet one chair sits empty this year, the bills on the counter have not gone away, and the doctor still has not called back. Somewhere between the blessing and the first bite, you wonder how anyone can say thank you when life feels this heavy. If that is where you are as November begins, this devotional is for you.

Most lists of Bible verses about gratitude are beautiful, but they can feel like they were written for people whose lives are going well. The surprising thing is that many of the strongest words of thanks in Scripture were spoken by people in prison, in hunger, in sickness, and in national disaster. Their thanksgiving was not a denial of pain. It was a decision to keep looking at God while the pain was still present.

In the pages below we will walk slowly through a handful of those passages and the stories behind them. Then we will turn them into simple habits for your mornings, your family table, and your Sabbath. You do not have to feel thankful to begin. You only have to be willing to take the next small step.

## The short answer

The Bible does not ask us to be thankful for every painful thing that happens. It asks us to give thanks in every situation, because God is still good, still present, and still working in it. Paul wrote, "In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you" (1 Thessalonians 5:18). Notice the small word "in." Gratitude in hard times is not pretending the hard thing is good; it is remembering that God has not left us inside it.

> "In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you." 1 Thessalonians 5:18, KJV

That verse sits beside two other short commands in the same passage, to rejoice and to pray continually (1 Thessalonians 5:16 to 17). Together they describe a heart that keeps turning toward God all day long. Thankfulness, in other words, is less like a feeling that visits us once a year and more like a direction we choose again and again.

**What biblical gratitude is not**
- It is not pretending you are fine
- It is not thanking God for evil or abuse
- It is not a test you fail when you cry
- It is trusting that God is good while you wait

## Thankful in prison: Paul and the Philippians

Paul wrote the letter to the Philippians while he was a prisoner. He tells his readers that "my bonds in Christ are manifest in all the palace, and in all other places" (Philippians 1:13). He did not know how his case would end. Yet this short letter is full of joy, and it contains one of the best loved invitations to grateful prayer in the whole Bible.

> "Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus." Philippians 4:6 to 7, KJV

"Be careful for nothing" means do not be anxious about anything. Paul does not tell the Philippians to stop asking God for help. He tells them to bring every request, and to wrap those requests in thanksgiving. The promise that follows is not that every problem will vanish, but that God's peace will stand guard over the heart and mind.

A few verses later Paul adds, "I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content" (Philippians 4:11). The word "learned" is a gift to anyone who finds gratitude hard. Paul was not born content. He grew into it through seasons of plenty and seasons of hunger (Philippians 4:12), and so can we.

## When the fields are empty: Habakkuk's song

The prophet Habakkuk lived in a frightening time. His book opens with honest complaints to God about violence and injustice, and God answers that the Chaldeans, the armies of Babylon, are coming (Habakkuk 1:6). Habakkuk does not hide his fear. By the end of the book, though, he sings one of the most courageous songs of thanks in Scripture.

> "Although the fig tree shall not blossom, neither shall fruit be in the vines; the labour of the olive shall fail, and the fields shall yield no meat; the flock shall be cut off from the fold, and there shall be no herd in the stalls: Yet I will rejoice in the LORD, I will joy in the God of my salvation." Habakkuk 3:17 to 18, KJV

For a farming people, this list describes total loss: no fruit, no oil, no grain, no animals. Habakkuk is not grateful because the harvest came in. He is grateful because the God of his salvation had not gone anywhere. His very next line says, "The LORD God is my strength" (Habakkuk 3:19).

## Entering His gates: the song of Psalm 100

Psalm 100 carries a simple title in the King James Version: "A Psalm of praise." It is only five verses long, and it invites "all ye lands" to come into God's presence with joy. The psalm pictures worshipers walking through the gates and into the courts of God's house, and it gives them words for that walk. For us, it shows that thanksgiving is the doorway into worship.

> "Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise: be thankful unto him, and bless his name. For the LORD is good; his mercy is everlasting; and his truth endureth to all generations." Psalm 100:4 to 5, KJV

Look at the reason the psalm gives for thanks. It is not "because life is easy" but "for the LORD is good." His mercy is everlasting and His truth lasts through every generation, including yours. Even the book of Lamentations, written in grief over a ruined city, holds on to the same hope: "They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness" (Lamentations 3:23).

## The one who turned back: the ten lepers

As Jesus traveled toward Jerusalem, ten men with leprosy met Him and "stood afar off" (Luke 17:12). They cried out, "Jesus, Master, have mercy on us" (Luke 17:13). Jesus told them to show themselves to the priests, and "as they went, they were cleansed" (Luke 17:14). All ten received the miracle, but the story does not end there.

- 10 : men cleansed on the road
- 1 : turned back to give thanks
- 9 : never came back

> "And one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, and with a loud voice glorified God, And fell down on his face at his feet, giving him thanks: and he was a Samaritan." Luke 17:15 to 16, KJV

The man who returned was a Samaritan, an outsider to many of the people around Jesus. Jesus asked, "Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine?" (Luke 17:17). Then He said to the grateful man, "Arise, go thy way: thy faith hath made thee whole" (Luke 17:19). Nine received healing for their skin, but the one who came back received something deeper: a face to face encounter with the Healer Himself.

## What gratitude does in us

Scripture calls us to thanksgiving because God deserves it, but it also shapes the person who gives it. Researchers have noticed something similar. Harvard Health Publishing reported on a 2024 study of more than 49,000 older women in the Nurses' Health Study, which found that women in the top third for gratitude had a 9% lower risk of dying over the next four years than women in the bottom third. The authors are careful to say the study shows an association, not proof, and that the women studied may not represent everyone.

We do not give thanks to live longer, and gratitude is never a cure for grief or illness. Still, it is encouraging to see careful research point in the same direction as the psalmist who said, "It is a good thing to give thanks unto the LORD" (Psalm 92:1). That psalm has a meaningful title too. It is "A Psalm or Song for the sabbath day."

## Gratitude in every season: practical habits

Gratitude grows like Paul's contentment did, through practice. Here is a simple comparison of how hard seasons and good seasons can both become places of thanks. You do not need to do all of these at once. Choose one and start this week.

| Season | What thanks can sound like | A verse to hold |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Grief or loss | Lord, thank You that I am not alone in this | Lamentations 3:23 |
| Money worries | Thank You for today's bread, and I trust You with tomorrow | Philippians 4:6 to 7 |
| Sickness | Thank You for every caring hand, and for Your peace tonight | Psalm 100:5 |
| A season of plenty | Help me remember You are the giver of every good thing | Deuteronomy 8:10 |

### At the family table

Moses told Israel, "When thou hast eaten and art full, then thou shalt bless the LORD thy God for the good land which he hath given thee" (Deuteronomy 8:10). The table has always been a place to remember God's goodness. This November, try going around the table once a week and letting each person name one thing they are thankful for, even small children. On hard weeks, give everyone permission to say something honest first and then one thing they still thank God for.

Related: [Five Ways to Build Faith at the Dinner Table](https://shekinahsda.org/blog/five-ways-to-build-faith-at-the-dinner-table/)

### Every Sabbath as a weekly Thanksgiving

Thanksgiving Day comes once a year, but God gave us a day of thanks every week. The Seventh-day Adventist Fundamental Belief 20 describes the Sabbath as "a day of delightful communion with God and one another" and "a celebration of God's creative and redemptive acts." When sunset arrives on Friday, you might light a candle, read Psalm 92 together, and name the ways God carried your family through the week. At Shekinah, our church family also shares a meal after the Sabbath service, and there are few better places to practice gratitude than around a shared table.

- Wake with one thanks : Before checking your phone, thank God for one specific thing
- Pray with thanksgiving : Name a blessing before each request, as Philippians 4:6 teaches
- Turn back : Like the Samaritan, thank God when a prayer is answered
- Say it out loud : Thank a person who has helped you this week
- Close the week well : Use Friday sunset to remember what God has done

### Gratitude across languages and generations

Our worship at Shekinah is in Kreyòl and English, and a heartfelt "mèsi, Senyè" reaches heaven just as surely as "thank You, Lord." Many Haitian families, in Haiti and across the diaspora, carry memories of real loss, including the earthquake that struck on January 12, 2010. Giving thanks in those memories does not mean anyone should be expected to be strong all the time or to hide their tears. It means bringing the whole story, the sorrow and the mercy, to the God who holds both. Gratitude that has walked through hardship is often the kind that speaks most deeply to the next generation.

## When thankfulness feels impossible

Some seasons are so dark that the words will not come. The Bible makes room for that, too, with whole psalms of lament. If you cannot say thank you yet, begin by telling God the truth about how you feel, as Habakkuk did, and ask Him to help you see one sign of His care.

Remember Paul and Silas, beaten and locked in stocks in Philippi. "And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them" (Acts 16:25). Their song did not come before midnight; it came in it. Your thanks, even if it is quiet and trembling, may be the very thing someone else near you needs to hear.

## Questions people ask

### What does the Bible say about giving thanks in hard times?

The Bible says to give thanks in every situation, not for every painful thing, because God is still good, still present, and still working in it. Paul wrote in 1 Thessalonians 5:18 that "In every thing give thanks," and the small word "in" makes all the difference. Gratitude in hard times is not pretending the hard thing is good. It is remembering that God has not left us inside it.

### Do I have to thank God for the bad things that happen?

No, biblical gratitude never asks you to thank God for evil, abuse, or the painful thing itself. Scripture asks us to give thanks in every circumstance, trusting that God is good while we wait. Gratitude is not pretending you are fine, and it is not a test you fail when you cry. The prophet Habakkuk shows the way, because he rejoiced in the God of his salvation while the fields were still empty (Habakkuk 3:17 to 18).

### What Bible verse says to give thanks in everything?

The Bible verse that tells us to give thanks in everything is 1 Thessalonians 5:18, which reads in the King James Version, "In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you." It sits beside two other short commands in 1 Thessalonians 5:16 to 17, to rejoice and to pray continually. Philippians 4:6 also asks us to bring every request to God with thanksgiving. Together these passages describe a heart that keeps turning toward God all day long.

### What should I do when I cannot feel thankful?

When you cannot feel thankful, begin by telling God the truth about how you feel, as the prophet Habakkuk did, and ask Him to help you see one sign of His care. The Bible makes room for that honesty with whole psalms of lament. You do not have to feel thankful to begin, because gratitude grows through practice, just as Paul said he had "learned" contentment in Philippians 4:11. Like Paul and Silas singing at midnight in Acts 16:25, even a quiet and trembling thank you is a real offering to God.

## Reflection questions

Take a few quiet minutes with these questions, alone or with your family. Which of the people in these passages, Paul, Habakkuk, the psalmist, or the Samaritan, feels most like you right now, and why? What is one thing God has done for you this year that you have never stopped to thank Him for? Who in your life needs to hear your thanks before Thanksgiving Day arrives?

## A word of encouragement

You do not have to wait until everything is fixed to be grateful, and you do not have to pretend everything is fixed in order to give thanks. God's mercy is new this morning, and His faithfulness will still be there tonight. The same Jesus who welcomed one thankful man at His feet welcomes you, whatever this season holds. Every small "thank You" is a step toward Him, and He is never too far away to hear it.

## A prayer

Father in heaven, thank You that Your mercy is everlasting and Your truth endures to all generations. In this season, some of us are rejoicing and some of us are hurting, and You see each heart. Teach us, like Paul, to learn contentment, and like the Samaritan, to turn back and thank You. Fill our tables, our homes, and our Sabbaths with gratitude, and let Your peace guard our hearts in Jesus. In His name we pray, Amen.

## Your next step

If this season is heavy for you, you do not have to carry it alone. Our church family would be honored to pray with you and for you, and you can share as much or as little as you like. Share a request through our prayer request page today, and know that a church family in Alvarado is lifting your name to God. You are always welcome to join us for Sabbath worship at 205 E Carver St, too.

- Source: [Jesus Cleanses Ten Lepers, Luke 17 (KJV)](https://www.christianity.com/bible/kjv/luke/17-11-17)

# Pikliz: The Spicy Haitian Slaw That Brightens Every Sabbath Plate

URL: https://shekinahsda.org/blog/pikliz-the-spicy-haitian-slaw/
Category: Recipes
Author: Josephine Pierre
Published: 2026-10-26

Make an original, plant based pikliz with a milder option, learn how to keep it safe and crisp in the fridge, and bring it to your Sabbath and Thanksgiving tables.


Picture a Sabbath lunch after a long, joyful morning of worship. The rice and beans are steaming, the plantains are golden, and the whole table smells like home. Then someone opens the refrigerator, sets down a jar of bright orange and white slaw, and the plate suddenly feels complete. That little jar is pikliz, and for many Haitian families a meal simply does not feel finished without it.

Maybe you grew up with pikliz and never learned to make it yourself. Maybe you are new to Haitian food and keep hearing friends talk about that spicy cabbage in the jar. Or maybe Thanksgiving is coming, someone asked you to bring a side dish, and you want something fresh to balance all the rich food. Whatever brought you here, you are in the right kitchen.

In this article we will share an original, fully plant based pikliz recipe with a milder option for children and tender palates. We will also cover the questions people ask most, like how long pikliz lasts, whether it is fermented, and what to eat with it. Because this is a condiment made with very hot peppers and raw vegetables, we will take time on food safety, using guidance from poison control, university extension services, and FoodSafety.gov.

## The short answer

Pikliz is a Haitian condiment of thinly shredded cabbage, carrots, onion, bell pepper, garlic, and hot peppers, covered in vinegar and left to steep in the refrigerator. It is ready to eat in about a day and tastes even better after two or three days. Kept cold in a clean jar with the vegetables under the vinegar, it will last for weeks, though it is a refrigerator food and never a shelf stable canned product. Its heat comes from scotch bonnet peppers, called piman bouk in Kreyòl, and you can control that heat completely.

- 1 day : Until your pikliz is ready to eat
- 40°F : Or colder for your refrigerator
- 3 months : Longest fridge time in extension guidance

## What pikliz is and where it comes from

### A condiment at the heart of the Haitian table

Researchers writing in the Journal of Ethnic Foods describe pikliz as a condiment made from shredded cabbage and carrot with a generous amount of hot pepper and spices, all immersed in vinegar or lemon juice. They note that it has long been prepared at the household level in Haiti and that many Haitian dishes are not considered complete without a portion of pikliz beside them. The same study describes pikliz as a symbol of Haitian identity for families in Haiti and abroad. Today you can even find commercial jars in many American supermarkets, but nothing quite compares to a batch made in your own kitchen.

Many people know pikliz as the partner to fried meats, and it is true that it is often served that way. Yet the heart of pikliz has always been vegetables, vinegar, and pepper. That makes it a natural fit for Adventist kitchens, where many of us enjoy plant based meals. A spoonful of pikliz brings brightness and crunch to beans, rice, plantains, and vegetable patties just as well.

### Is pikliz fermented?

The answer depends on who you ask and how the jar is made. The researchers in the Journal of Ethnic Foods describe some natural fermentation taking place as pikliz sits, with helpful bacteria adding acid and flavor over time. Many home recipes, including ours, get their sourness from vinegar right from the first day, so they work like a quick refrigerator pickle. Either way, the recipe below is meant to be kept cold from the moment you fill the jar.

## The recipe: Shekinah style pikliz

This is our own family style version, written to be simple and forgiving. Use a sharp knife or a mandoline to slice the cabbage as thin as you can, because thin shreds soak up the vinegar and stay pleasantly crisp. If you use a mandoline, always use the hand guard. The amounts below fill roughly two quart jars, depending on how firmly you pack them.

| Ingredient | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| Green cabbage, cored and very thinly shredded | 1 small head, about 2 pounds |
| Carrots, cut into thin matchsticks or coarsely grated | 2 medium |
| Red onion or shallots, thinly sliced | 1 small onion or 2 shallots |
| Red or green bell pepper, cut in thin strips | 1/2 pepper |
| Scotch bonnet peppers (piman bouk), thinly sliced | 2 to 4, or 1 seeded for mild |
| Garlic cloves, thinly sliced | 4 |
| Whole cloves | 6 |
| Black peppercorns | 1 teaspoon |
| Fine salt | 1 1/2 teaspoons |
| Distilled white vinegar labeled 5% acidity | 3 to 4 cups, enough to cover |
| Fresh lime juice (optional) | Juice of 1 lime |

### Choosing your heat

Is pikliz spicy? Traditional pikliz is very spicy, because scotch bonnets are fiery little peppers and close cousins of the habanero. Much of their heat sits in the pale inner ribs and the seeds, so removing them tames the jar a great deal. For a gentle family batch, use one scotch bonnet with the seeds and ribs removed, and let the jar sit a day before tasting.

If you want pikliz without scotch bonnet, a habanero is the closest stand in, with similar fruity heat. For a truly mild jar that children can enjoy, use a seeded jalapeño or simply leave the hot pepper out and add a little extra black pepper. You can always slip another sliced pepper into the jar later, but you cannot take heat back out once it is there.

### Method

- Wash and prep : Wash hands, rinse vegetables, and shred everything thin
- Gloves on : Slice the hot peppers wearing gloves
- Toss : Mix vegetables with salt, garlic, cloves, and peppercorns
- Pack and cover : Pack into clean jars and pour in vinegar to cover
- Chill : Refrigerate right away and wait at least one day

Start by washing your hands and rinsing the cabbage, carrots, onion, and peppers under running water. Shred and slice everything into a large clean bowl, then put on gloves before you cut the scotch bonnets. Add the hot peppers, garlic, cloves, peppercorns, and salt, and toss well with a clean spoon or with your gloved hands until the colors are evenly mixed.

Pack the vegetables into clean glass jars, pressing down gently so they settle. Pour in the vinegar until every shred is fully covered, add the lime juice if you are using it, and slide a clean spoon down the sides to release any air bubbles. Close the jars with clean lids and place them in the refrigerator right away. After about a day the pikliz is ready, and after two or three days the flavors deepen and the heat spreads through the whole jar.

## Keeping pikliz safe and crisp

### Handling hot peppers

The burning oil in hot peppers is called capsaicin, and it does not wash off easily. Poison Control advises wearing rubber, latex, or nitrile gloves when working with hot peppers and not touching your face or eyes afterward. If pepper does get into your eyes, they recommend rinsing with plenty of warm water for about fifteen minutes. If someone has trouble breathing or chest discomfort, call 911, and for other questions you can reach Poison Control at 1 800 222 1222.

### Clean jars, cold fridge, clean spoons

FoodSafety.gov recommends washing cutting boards, utensils, and countertops with hot, soapy water and rinsing produce under running water without soap. It also says your refrigerator should be set to 40°F or below, and that perishable foods should be refrigerated within two hours. That matters for pikliz, which has no cooking step to protect it. Always serve from the jar with a clean, dry spoon, never with a fork that has touched someone's plate, and keep the vegetables pushed down under the vinegar.

The vinegar matters too. The National Center for Home Food Preservation's refrigerator pickle lesson calls for vinegar of 5% acidity. We use the vinegar full strength and do not water it down. Look for the acidity on the label before you buy.

### How long does pikliz last?

Oregon State University's Food Hero refrigerator pickled vegetables recipe says to store the jars only in the refrigerator and to use them within three months. The National Center for Home Food Preservation gives the same three month window for its refrigerator pickles. Those are tested recipes, and ours is a home recipe, so we suggest enjoying your pikliz within about a month, when it is also at its crunchiest. If you ever see mold, a slimy texture, or an off smell, throw the whole jar away.

**Pikliz food safety at a glance**
- Wear gloves to cut hot peppers and keep hands away from eyes
- Use clean jars, lids, bowls, and spoons
- Use vinegar labeled 5% acidity at full strength
- Keep vegetables under the vinegar and the jar at 40°F or colder
- Store only in the refrigerator, never on the pantry shelf
- Enjoy within about a month and discard if anything looks or smells wrong

## What to eat with pikliz

So what do you eat with pikliz? In Haiti it is famously served beside fried dishes, but it shines with plant based foods too. Spoon it next to banann peze, the twice fried green plantains, or over a warm plate of diri ak pwa. It is wonderful tucked into a sandwich with black bean patties, served alongside baked sweet potatoes, or stirred into a simple bowl of brown rice and greens.

Related: [Diri ak Pwa the Healthy Way](https://shekinahsda.org/blog/diri-ak-pwa-the-healthy-way/)

### For the Thanksgiving table

Thanksgiving tables are often heavy with soft, rich foods, and pikliz offers exactly what they need: crunch, acid, and a little fire. A small bowl beside the stuffing, sweet potatoes, and plant based mains lets each guest add as much as they like. If you are carrying it to a family gathering, keep the jar in a cooler and put leftovers back in the refrigerator within two hours. Consider bringing one mild jar and one spicy jar, clearly marked, so nobody gets surprised.

## Good food for the body God gave us

Cabbage is a humble vegetable with a lot to offer. North Carolina State Extension notes that one cup of raw green cabbage has about 22 calories and 2 grams of fiber and provides 36% of the daily value for vitamin C. Harvard's Nutrition Source lists cruciferous vegetables like cabbage, along with bell peppers, among good food sources of vitamin C, and notes that high heat and long cooking can break the vitamin down. Pikliz is never cooked, though the exact nutrients in a finished jar will vary, so think of it as a flavorful way to eat more vegetables rather than a health food with promised numbers.

Our Seventh-day Adventist Fundamental Belief 22, Christian Behavior, reminds us that our bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit and that we should care for them intelligently, adopting the most healthful diet possible. That is not a call to bland food. Pikliz shows how a few vegetables, a little salt, and good vinegar can make a plate both nourishing and full of joy. Because it does contain salt, a spoonful or two at a time is plenty.

## Flavor, salt, and the goodness of God

Scripture often uses taste to teach us about God. David wrote a psalm of praise that invites everyone to experience God's goodness for themselves. It is one of the warmest invitations in the whole Bible.

> "O taste and see that the LORD is good: blessed is the man that trusteth in him." Psalm 34:8, KJV

David was not writing about food, but he chose the language of taste because some things must be experienced to be understood. Jesus did something similar when He told His followers, "Ye are the salt of the earth" (Matthew 5:13), and Paul urged believers to let their speech be "alway with grace, seasoned with salt" (Colossians 4:6). Just as a little pikliz brightens an entire plate, a life touched by Christ can bring warmth and flavor to the people around it. These are pictures, not recipes, yet they remind us that even our ordinary meals can point us to the One who made every good thing.

## Questions people ask

### What is pikliz made of?

Pikliz is made of thinly shredded cabbage, carrots, onion, bell pepper, garlic, and hot scotch bonnet peppers, covered in vinegar and left to steep in the refrigerator. Our Shekinah style recipe also adds whole cloves, black peppercorns, salt, and an optional squeeze of fresh lime juice. Researchers writing in the Journal of Ethnic Foods describe pikliz as shredded cabbage and carrot with plenty of hot pepper and spices immersed in vinegar or lemon juice. For safety and flavor, use distilled white vinegar labeled 5% acidity at full strength.

### Is pikliz spicy?

Traditional pikliz is very spicy, because it is made with scotch bonnet peppers, called piman bouk in Kreyòl, which are close cousins of the habanero. Much of the heat sits in the pale inner ribs and the seeds, so removing them tames the jar a great deal. For a mild family batch, use one seeded scotch bonnet or a seeded jalapeño, or leave the hot pepper out and add a little extra black pepper. You can always slip more pepper into the jar later, but you cannot take heat back out.

### Do you have to refrigerate pikliz?

Yes, homemade pikliz must always be kept in the refrigerator at 40°F or colder, because it is a refrigerator pickle and never a shelf stable canned product. FoodSafety.gov recommends setting your refrigerator to 40°F or below and refrigerating perishable foods within two hours. Oregon State University's Food Hero recipe for refrigerator pickled vegetables also says to store the jars only in the refrigerator. Keep the vegetables pushed under the vinegar and always serve with a clean, dry spoon.

### How soon can you eat pikliz after making it?

Pikliz is ready to eat after about one day in the refrigerator, and it tastes even better after two or three days. During that time the vinegar soaks into the thin shreds of cabbage and carrot, the flavors deepen, and the heat of the scotch bonnets spreads through the whole jar. Slicing the cabbage as thin as you can helps it absorb the vinegar while staying pleasantly crisp. For the best crunch, enjoy a homemade jar within about a month.

## Reflection questions

When you share a meal this week, how could you make room for gratitude before the first bite? Who in your life might need the kind of encouragement that brightens a hard day, the way pikliz brightens a plate? And as Thanksgiving approaches, what simple dish could you prepare and share as an act of kindness for a neighbor or someone eating alone?

## A word of encouragement

You do not need to be a perfect cook to bless your family. A jar of pikliz takes about thirty minutes of chopping and a little patience, yet it can carry the taste of home to a homesick friend or welcome a guest to your table. God sees the care you put into everyday things, and nothing done in love is ever small. As you slice, pack, and share, may your kitchen become a place where people feel at home and taste His goodness.

## A prayer

Lord, thank You for the gift of food and for the simple things that make our tables bright. Thank You for cabbage and carrots, for peppers and spices, and for the hands that prepare them. Help us care for the bodies You have given us, and make our lives a seasoning of grace to everyone we meet. We ask this in the name of Jesus, amen.

## Your next step

If you would like to share a meal with a church family that loves Haitian food, we would be glad to welcome you. Shekinah Haitian Seventh-day Adventist Church meets at 205 E Carver St in Alvarado, Texas, with Sabbath School on Saturday at 10:00 AM and Divine Service at 11:00 AM, and our worship is in Kreyòl and English. After the service our church family shares a meal together, and there is always room for one more at the table. Visit our Plan Your Visit page to learn what to expect.
